name: 孔子
oneLiner: 以「仁」为最高理想，把道德从庙堂拉回人与人相处的日常。
oneLinerEn: Made ren (benevolence) the highest ideal, bringing morality back to daily human relations.
bio: 周游列国而行道不遇，晚年归鲁讲学、删述六经，其言行由弟子辑为《论语》，奠定东亚文明的伦理底色。
bioEn: He traveled among states seeking a ruler to reform, then taught and edited classics; his sayings became the Analects, the ethical bedrock of East Asia.

ideas.v: 推己及人的不忍人之心，是礼的根基。
ideas.vEn: Humaneness extended to others; the root of ritual.

ideas.v: 过犹不及，执两用中。
ideas.vEn: Avoid extremes; hold the middle.

ideas.v: 打破贵族垄断，首开私学。
ideas.vEn: Opened learning beyond the aristocracy.

quotes.q: 己所不欲，勿施于人。
quotes.qEn: Do not impose on others what you yourself do not desire.

name: 老子
oneLiner: 道可道非常道——主张言说之外的自然之道与无为而治。
oneLinerEn: The Dao that can be told is not the constant Dao — nature's way and non-action in governance.
bio: 传说为周守藏室之史，见周室衰微，西出函谷关，应关令尹喜之请著《道德经》五千言。
bioEn: Reputedly an archivist who, disillusioned with the declining Zhou, wrote the Dao De Jing at a border pass before vanishing west.

ideas.v: 万物依其本然运行，不假外求。
ideas.vEn: All things move by their own nature.

ideas.v: 不妄为、因势利导，而非不为。
ideas.vEn: Act without forcing; not inaction but non-interference.

ideas.v: 水善利万物而不争。
ideas.vEn: Water benefits all and contends with none.

quotes.q: 上善若水，水善利万物而不争。
quotes.qEn: The highest good is like water, which nourishes all things without strife.

name: 柏拉图
oneLiner: 可见世界是理型的影子，真知在于以理性回忆永恒。
oneLinerEn: The visible world is a shadow of the Forms; true knowledge is rational recollection.
bio: 苏格拉底弟子，创办雅典学园（Academy），以对话体写下大量著作，奠定西方形而上学与政治哲学。
bioEn: A student of Socrates, he founded the Academy in Athens and wrote dialogues that founded Western metaphysics and political philosophy.

ideas.v: 完美的共相独立存在，感官世界只是摹本。
ideas.vEn: Perfect universals exist apart; the sensible world is a copy.

ideas.v: 被囚者误把影子当真实。
ideas.vEn: Prisoners mistake shadows for reality.

ideas.v: 唯有爱智者应执掌城邦。
ideas.vEn: Only lovers of wisdom should rule.

quotes.q: 未经省察的人生不值得过。
quotes.qEn: The unexamined life is not worth living.

name: 亚里士多德
oneLiner: 从观察出发，以四因与中道解释自然、灵魂与政治。
oneLinerEn: From observation, explains nature, soul and politics via four causes and the mean.
bio: 柏拉图弟子、亚历山大大帝之师，创立吕克昂学园，著作涵盖逻辑、自然、伦理与政治学，是中世纪学术的骨架。
bioEn: Student of Plato and tutor to Alexander, he founded the Lyceum; his works across logic, nature, ethics and politics became the skeleton of medieval learning.

ideas.v: 质料、形式、动力、目的解释事物。
ideas.vEn: Matter, form, agent, purpose explain things.

ideas.v: 过度与不及之间恰好处。
ideas.vEn: The right measure between excess and defect.

ideas.v: 在具体处境中择善的能力。
ideas.vEn: The ability to choose well in concrete situations.

quotes.q: 人是政治的动物。
quotes.qEn: Man is by nature a political animal.

name: 康德
oneLiner: 调和理性与经验，并以绝对命令为道德立法。
oneLinerEn: Synthesizes reason and experience and legislates morality by the categorical imperative.
bio: 终身未离柯尼斯堡，以三大批判重塑认识论、伦理学与美学，被誉为「哲学界的哥白尼革命」。
bioEn: He never left Königsberg yet, with his three Critiques, reshaped epistemology, ethics and aesthetics — a 'Copernican revolution' in philosophy.

ideas.v: 心智主动构造经验。
ideas.vEn: The mind actively structures experience.

ideas.v: 只按你同时愿意成为普遍法则的准则行动。
ideas.vEn: Act only on maxims you could will universal law.

ideas.v: 切勿把人仅当手段。
ideas.vEn: Never treat humanity merely as means.

quotes.q: 位我上者灿烂星空，道德律令在我心中。
quotes.qEn: Two things fill the mind with awe: the starry heavens above and the moral law within.

name: 马克思
oneLiner: 以历史唯物主义诊断资本主义：剥削源于对剩余价值的占有。
oneLinerEn: Historical materialism diagnoses capitalism: exploitation lies in appropriating surplus value.
bio: 与恩格斯合著《共产党宣言》，穷毕生之力写《资本论》，其学说深刻塑造了 20 世纪的政治版图。
bioEn: With Engels he wrote the Manifesto and spent his life on Capital; his thought reshaped 20th-century politics.

ideas.v: 生产方式决定社会结构。
ideas.vEn: The mode of production shapes society.

ideas.v: 利润来自对劳动的 unpaid 占有。
ideas.vEn: Profit arises from unpaid labor.

ideas.v: 劳动者与产品、劳动、类本质相疏离。
ideas.vEn: Workers are estranged from product, act and species-being.

quotes.q: 哲学家们只是用不同的方式解释世界，问题在于改变世界。
quotes.qEn: Philosophers have only interpreted the world; the point is to change it.

name: 尼采
oneLiner: 宣告「上帝已死」，呼唤人超越自身、成为超人。
oneLinerEn: Declares 'God is dead' and calls humans to overcome themselves into the Übermensch.
bio: 曾任 Basel 古典语文学教授，因病退隐著述，以格言体犀利批判基督教道德与虚无主义。
bioEn: A classical philology professor who, ill and reclusive, wrote aphoristic critiques of Christian morality and nihilism.

ideas.v: 传统价值失稳，人须重新立法。
ideas.vEn: Traditional values collapse; humans must re-legislate.

ideas.v: 生命本质是扩张与自我超越的冲动。
ideas.vEn: Life is the drive to expand and surpass.

ideas.v: 若此生无限重复，你能否说「我愿意」？
ideas.vEn: If this life recurred forever, could you say 'I will it'?

quotes.q: 那些杀不死我的，使我更强大。
quotes.qEn: What does not kill me makes me stronger.

name: 休谟
oneLiner: 观念皆来自印象，因果只是习惯的恒常联结。
oneLinerEn: Ideas derive from impressions; causation is mere habitual conjunction.
bio: 苏格兰启蒙核心人物，以《人性论》《人类理解研究》把经验主义推至怀疑论边缘，自谓「唤醒」了康德。
bioEn: A central Scottish Enlightenment figure whose Treatise and Enquiry pushed empiricism toward skepticism and, he said, 'awoke' Kant.

ideas.v: 观念是印象的黯淡副本。
ideas.vEn: Ideas are faint copies of impressions.

ideas.v: 我们从未看见「必然」，只见恒常接续。
ideas.vEn: We never see necessity, only constant sequence.

ideas.v: 自我是一束流动的知觉。
ideas.vEn: The self is a bundle of fleeting perceptions.

quotes.q: 理性是激情的奴隶。
quotes.qEn: Reason is, and ought only to be, the slave of the passions.

name: 萨特
oneLiner: 存在先于本质——人先被抛入世界，再以选择自我定义。
oneLinerEn: Existence precedes essence — thrown into the world, we define ourselves by choice.
bio: 法国哲人与作家，二战后成为存在主义旗手，主张人在荒诞中须为自己与全体人类负责。
bioEn: French philosopher and writer who became the postwar voice of existentialism: in absurdity, we bear responsibility for ourselves and all.

ideas.v: 人先存在，再借行动成为某类人。
ideas.vEn: We exist first, then become via action.

ideas.v: 自由选择即选择人类整体形象。
ideas.vEn: To choose freely is to choose for all humanity.

ideas.v: 不诿过于处境，直面自己的选择。
ideas.vEn: Own your choices instead of blaming circumstance.

quotes.q: 人被判处自由。
quotes.qEn: Man is condemned to be free.

name: 王阳明
oneLiner: 主张「心即理」「知行合一」「致良知」，把道德践履拉回本心。
oneLinerEn: Held that 'the mind is principle', knowledge and action are one, and we should extend innate knowing.
bio: 明代大儒与军事家，平宁王之乱，于龙场悟道，创立阳明学，影响东亚近世行动伦理。
bioEn: A Ming statesman-general who, after his epiphany at Longchang, founded Yangming learning, shaping East Asian activist ethics.

ideas.v: 不必外求，天理即在心。
ideas.vEn: Principle is not outside; it is in the mind.

ideas.v: 真知必发为行，不行只是未知。
ideas.vEn: True knowing issues in action; otherwise it is not yet known.

ideas.v: 在事上磨练本有的道德判断。
ideas.vEn: Cultivate the native moral sense through affairs.

quotes.q: 你未看此花时，此花与汝心同归于寂。
quotes.qEn: Until you look, the flower and your mind alike are idle.

name: 笛卡尔
oneLiner: 以普遍怀疑求得「我思故我在」，为近代哲学与科学奠基。
oneLinerEn: By radical doubt he reached 'I think therefore I am', grounding modern philosophy and science.
bio: 数学家与哲学家，创立解析几何，主张以清晰分明的观念重建知识大厦，开启近代认识论。
bioEn: Mathematician-philosopher who founded analytic geometry and rebuilt knowledge on clear distinct ideas, opening modern epistemology.

ideas.v: 凡可疑者皆暂悬置。
ideas.vEn: Set aside whatever can be doubted.

ideas.v: 怀疑本身证明思考者存在。
ideas.vEn: The very act of doubt proves the thinker exists.

ideas.v: 心灵与广延之物本质不同。
ideas.vEn: Mind and extended matter are of different essence.

quotes.q: 我思故我在。
quotes.qEn: I think, therefore I am.

name: 密尔
oneLiner: 以最大幸福为原则，并区分高级与低级快乐，且力主自由。
oneLinerEn: Championed the greatest-happiness principle, distinguishing higher from lower pleasures, and liberty.
bio: 由父亲严教成才，毕生推动功利主义、女性平权与言论自由，是 19 世纪自由主义标杆。
bioEn: Educated rigorously by his father, he advanced utilitarianism, women's equality and free speech — a 19th-c. liberal benchmark.

ideas.v: 行为的对错看总体福祉净值。
ideas.vEn: Right acts maximize net well-being.

ideas.v: 宁愿做不满足的人，不做满足的猪。
ideas.vEn: Better a dissatisfied Socrates than a satisfied pig.

ideas.v: 仅当损害他人，国家方可干预。
ideas.vEn: The state may intervene only to prevent harm to others.

quotes.q: 个人的自由，以不伤害他人为界。
quotes.qEn: The liberty of one ends where harm to another begins.

name: 马可·奥勒留
oneLiner: 一位皇帝的自我劝诫：以控制二分在乱世中守住内心的安宁。
oneLinerEn: An emperor's self-counsel: keep inner peace amid turmoil via the dichotomy of control.
bio: 罗马「五贤帝」之末，戎马一生而夜夜自省，留下未打算出版的《沉思录》。
bioEn: The last of Rome's 'Five Good Emperors', he campaigned on the frontiers yet wrote nightly self-reflections never meant for print.

ideas.v: 只操心你能决定的。
ideas.vEn: Care only for what is up to you.

ideas.v: 接受必然，履行本分。
ideas.vEn: Accept necessity, do your part.

ideas.v: 过去与未来皆不在你手中。
ideas.vEn: Past and future are not yours to grip.

quotes.q: 你拥有控制你思想的力量，外界无法动摇。
quotes.qEn: You have power over your mind — not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength.

name: 波伏瓦
school: 存在主义 / 女性主义
oneLiner: 以存在主义揭示「女人是被造成的」，开启现代女性主义理论。
oneLinerEn: Used existentialism to show 'one is not born a woman', launching modern feminist theory.
bio: 与萨特相伴一生而各自独立，以《第二性》《名士风流》把哲学写进性别与自由的现场。
bioEn: Lifelong companion of Sartre yet independent, she brought philosophy to questions of sex and freedom in The Second Sex and The Mandarins.

ideas.v: 女性被定义为相对于男性的「他者」。
ideas.vEn: Woman is defined as the Other relative to man.

ideas.v: 性别是历史与社会的产物。
ideas.vEn: Gender is made by history and society.

ideas.v: 人应超越既定角色，自我筹划。
ideas.vEn: One should transcend given roles and project oneself.

quotes.q: 女人不是天生的，而是被塑造成的。
quotes.qEn: One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman.

name: 庄子
oneLiner: 以逍遥与齐物破除外在束缚与是非对待，主张顺应天籁、与物为春。
oneLinerEn: With carefree wandering and the equality of things, he loosens every outward fetter and the yes/no of right and wrong.
bio: 战国道家代表，承老子而恣肆发挥；《庄子》以寓言写哲学，把自由精神推向极致，深深滋养了后世的文艺与心境。
bioEn: The great Daoist of the Warring States who pushed Laozi further; the Zhuangzi uses parables to radicalize spiritual freedom and shaped later literature and art.

ideas.v: 超越功名得失，与天地精神往来。
ideas.vEn: Transcend fame and gain; roam with the spirit of heaven and earth.

ideas.v: 是非、美丑、生死本无绝对分界。
ideas.vEn: Right/wrong, beauty/ugly, life/death have no fixed boundary.

ideas.v: 不材之木得以全生，利害相生。
ideas.vEn: The uncarved tree survives; use and uselessness intertwine.

quotes.q: 吾生也有涯，而知也无涯。
quotes.qEn: Life has a limit; knowledge has none.

name: 孟子
oneLiner: 主张性善与仁政，以「不忍人之心」为道德与政治的共同根基。
oneLinerEn: Argued for innate goodness and humane government, rooting both morality and politics in the 'heart that cannot bear others' suffering'.
bio: 战国儒家大宗，游说诸侯行王道、反霸道，高扬「民为贵」；其说经宋儒推尊为「亚圣」。
bioEn: A Warring-States Confucian who urged humane kingship over hegemony and declared 'the people are weightiest'; later honored as the Second Sage.

ideas.v: 恻隐、羞恶、辞让、是非，四端具足。
ideas.vEn: Compassion, shame, deference, discernment — four sprouts within.

ideas.v: 推不忍人之心以保民而王。
ideas.vEn: Extend the unforced heart to care for the people.

ideas.v: 配义与道，充塞于天地。
ideas.vEn: A spirit nourished by rightness and the Way.

quotes.q: 民为贵，社稷次之，君为轻。
quotes.qEn: The people are weightiest; the state comes next; the ruler is lightest.

name: 苏格拉底
oneLiner: 以「认识你自己」与诘问法揭露假知，把哲学转向对善与自我的省察。
oneLinerEn: With 'know yourself' and cross-examination he exposed false knowledge, turning philosophy to the examination of the good and the self.
bio: 雅典哲人，不立文字，借对话逼问前提交出「自知无知」；终以「败坏青年」获罪，饮鸩而亡，成为哲学生命的典范。
bioEn: An Athenian who wrote nothing but questioned citizens into contradiction, claiming only to know that he did not know; condemned and executed, he became philosophy's martyr.

ideas.v: 以追问暴露信念的内在矛盾。
ideas.vEn: Questioning that exposes contradiction in belief.

ideas.v: 无人有意作恶，恶出于无知。
ideas.vEn: No one errs willingly; evil stems from ignorance.

ideas.v: 不反思的生活不值得过。
ideas.vEn: The unexamined life is not worth living.

quotes.q: 我唯一知道的，是我一无所知。
quotes.qEn: I know that I do not know.

name: 洛克
oneLiner: 人心如白板(tabula rasa)，知识源于经验；为自由主义与宪政奠定基石。
oneLinerEn: The mind is a blank slate; knowledge comes from experience — and he laid the foundations of liberalism and constitutional government.
bio: 英国经验论奠基者，著《人类理解论》与《政府论》，主张自然权利与分权，深刻影响启蒙运动与近代宪政。
bioEn: Founder of British empiricism; his Essay and Two Treatises argued natural rights and separation of powers, shaping the Enlightenment and modern constitutions.

ideas.v: 心灵初如白纸，经验写入一切。
ideas.vEn: The mind begins blank; experience writes all.

ideas.v: 生命、自由、财产不可剥夺。
ideas.vEn: Life, liberty, property are inalienable.

ideas.v: 立法、行政相分以防专断。
ideas.vEn: Divide legislative and executive to check power.

quotes.q: 哪里没有法律，哪里就没有自由。
quotes.qEn: Where there is no law, there is no freedom.

name: 维特根斯坦
oneLiner: 前期主张语言描绘世界的逻辑图像，后期转向「意义即用法」，划出可说与不可说的界限。
oneLinerEn: Early work: language pictures the world's logical form. Late work: meaning is use — drawing the line between what can be said and what must be shown.
bio: 20世纪最具颠覆力的哲学家，前后期思想判若两人；《逻辑哲学论》与《哲学研究》各自开宗立派，影响语言哲学与心灵哲学。
bioEn: The most radical philosopher of the century; his Tractatus and Philosophical Investigations founded two distinct schools, reshaping language and mind.

ideas.v: 命题以逻辑结构映照事实。
ideas.vEn: Propositions mirror facts in logical structure.

ideas.v: 词的意义在其语言游戏中的用法。
ideas.vEn: A word's meaning is its use in the language-game.

ideas.v: 概念靠交叠相似连成网络。
ideas.vEn: Concepts link by overlapping similarities.

quotes.q: 凡不可言说者，必保持沉默。
quotes.qEn: Whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent.

name: 海德格尔
oneLiner: 重提「存在」之问，以「此在」(Dasein)揭示人与世界前理论的牵连，并追问技术的本质。
oneLinerEn: Revived the question of Being; through 'Dasein' he showed our pre-theoretical entanglement with the world, and later probed the essence of technology.
bio: 20世纪存在哲学巨擘，《存在与时间》开启此在的分析；晚年转向诗意栖居与技术批判，影响存在主义与后现代思潮。
bioEn: A towering figure of existential thought; Being and Time launched Dasein-analysis, while his later writings on poetry and technology shaped postmodernism.

ideas.v: 人是对自身存在有所领会的存在者。
ideas.vEn: The human being is the entity that understands its own being.

ideas.v: 人总已置身于世界之中。
ideas.vEn: We are always already thrown into a world.

ideas.v: 直面死亡才本真地领受自身。
ideas.vEn: Only facing death do we own our finite self.

quotes.q: 人，被抛入此世，并走向死亡。
quotes.qEn: Thrown into the world, we are underway toward death.

name: 托马斯·阿奎那
oneLiner: 把亚里士多德与基督教信仰熔于一炉，主张理性与启示并不矛盾。
oneLinerEn: Fused Aristotle with Christian faith, holding reason and revelation compatible.
bio: 以「五路论证」上帝存在、以自然法伦理学奠基道德，其《神学大全》成为中世纪思想的高峰。
bioEn: His Five Ways argued for God, his natural law grounded ethics, and the Summa Theologica crowned medieval thought.

ideas.v: 由运动与因果推出第一推动者。
ideas.vEn: Infers a first mover from motion and causation.

ideas.v: 道德根植于理性对人性目的的认识。
ideas.vEn: Morality rests on reason grasping human ends.

quotes.q: 对最高事物的一点点认识，胜于对琐物的确定知识。
quotes.qEn: A little knowledge of the highest things surpasses certainty in trifles.

name: 斯宾诺莎
oneLiner: 宣称神与自然是同一唯一实体，万物都在必然中展开。
oneLinerEn: Declared God and Nature one sole substance, with all things unfolding in necessity.
bio: 以几何学方法写作《伦理学》，否定人格神与自由意志，主张以理智之爱理解世界而获得自由。
bioEn: Writing the Ethics in geometric order, he denied a personal God and free will, finding freedom in understanding the world.

ideas.v: 只有一种实体，即神或自然。
ideas.vEn: One substance alone: God, or Nature.

ideas.v: 心灵与身体按同一必然律运行。
ideas.vEn: Mind and body run by one necessary order.

quotes.q: 不嘲笑，不哀痛，不憎恨，只理解。
quotes.qEn: Not to laugh, not to weep, not to hate — but to understand.

name: 朱熹
oneLiner: 集北宋理学之大成，以「存天理、去人欲」与格物穷理重塑儒学。
oneLinerEn: Synthesized Song learning, recasting Confucianism through principle, self-restraint and the investigation of things.
bio: 以《四书章句集注》将四书提升为儒学核心，其理气二元论成为后世科举正统与东亚士人精神的支柱。
bioEn: His variorum notes on the Four Books made them the canon; his li–qi framework became the exam orthodoxy of later East Asia.

ideas.v: 事物皆分统一普遍之理。
ideas.vEn: All things partake one universal principle.

ideas.v: 即物而穷其理以通全体。
ideas.vEn: Study each thing to exhaust its principle.

works.title: 四书章句集注
works.titleEn: Variorum Notes on the Four Books

quotes.q: 问渠那得清如许，为有源头活水来。
quotes.qEn: Why is it so clear? Because living water flows from its source.

sources.label: 《四书章句集注》
sources.labelEn: Collected Commentaries on the Four Books

name: 约翰·杜威
oneLiner: 把真理看作行动中有用的假设，主张从做中学与民主作为一种生活方式。
oneLinerEn: Treated truth as working hypotheses in action, urging learning by doing and democracy as a way of life.
bio: 以实验主义认识论与进步主义教育改革影响二十世纪，主张哲学应直面具体的人类问题而非经院玄想。
bioEn: His instrumentalism and progressive education shaped the twentieth century, pressing philosophy to face live human problems.

ideas.v: 观念是应对环境的工具，以效果验真。
ideas.vEn: Ideas are tools; their worth shows in consequences.

ideas.v: 教育在经验与反思的循环中发生。
ideas.vEn: Learning grows from an experience–reflection cycle.

quotes.q: 教育不是为生活做准备，教育本身就是生活。
quotes.qEn: Education is not preparation for life; education is life itself.

name: 阿尔贝·加缪
oneLiner: 真正严肃的哲学问题只有一个：自杀。他追问在一个无意义世界里值不值得活。
oneLinerEn: There is but one truly serious philosophical problem, suicide — is life worth living in a meaningless world?
bio: 以《西西弗神话》提出荒诞，以《局外人》写沉默的旁观者，主张在认清荒诞后仍反叛地、自由地活。
bioEn: The Myth of Sisyphus named the absurd, The Stranger its silent witness; he urged living on in revolt and freedom after facing it.

ideas.v: 人对意义的渴望与世界无回应之间的张力。
ideas.vEn: The tension between our hunger for meaning and the world's silence.

ideas.v: 不自杀也不寄望于彼岸，而是在推石上山中肯定生活。
ideas.vEn: Neither suicide nor hope, but affirming life in the endless task.

quotes.q: 应当想象西西弗是幸福的。
quotes.qEn: One must imagine Sisyphus happy.

name: 伊壁鸠鲁
oneLiner: 真正的快乐不是纵情声色，而是身体无痛、心灵宁静与真挚友谊。
oneLinerEn: True pleasure is not indulgence but a body free of pain, a tranquil mind and real friendship.
bio: 古希腊哲学家，在雅典的「花园」中与弟子共同生活、讲学。他把快乐确立为生活的目的，却将快乐理解为痛苦的缺席与心灵的安宁，主张节制欲望、研习自然、免除对神与死的恐惧。
bioEn: Ancient Greek philosopher who lived and taught with his followers in the Athenian 'Garden'. He made pleasure the aim of life yet defined it as the absence of pain and disturbance, urging moderated desires, the study of nature, and freedom from fear of the gods and of death.

ideas.v: 快乐即无痛与不扰，非感官的放纵。
ideas.vEn: Pleasure is freedom from pain and disturbance, not sensual excess.

ideas.v: 自然又必要的易满足，虚名的欲望无穷。
ideas.vEn: Natural and necessary desires are easily filled; empty ones are endless.

ideas.v: 我们在时死未至，死至时我已不在。
ideas.vEn: Where I am, death is not; where death is, I am not.

quotes.q: 不要破坏我们所拥有的，而是渴望我们所没有的，如此便不快乐。
quotes.qEn: Nothing is enough for the man to whom enough is too little.

name: 托马斯·霍布斯
oneLiner: 没有公共权力时人对人如狼，人们让渡权利给主权者以换取秩序与安全。
oneLinerEn: Without a common power people are wolves to one another; we hand rights to a sovereign to buy order and safety.
bio: 英国哲学家，著《利维坦》。他设想没有共同权力的「自然状态」是人人自危的战争，生活因而孤独、贫困而短寿；人们为求自保订立契约，把权力交给一个强大的主权者。他是近代政治哲学与社会契约论的奠基者之一。
bioEn: English philosopher, author of Leviathan. He imagined a 'state of nature' without a common power as a war of all against all that made life solitary, poor and short; to survive, people covenant to surrender their power to a strong sovereign. He is a founder of modern political philosophy and contract theory.

ideas.v: 无权威时人对人是狼，人人自危。
ideas.vEn: Without authority, every person is a wolf to every other.

ideas.v: 各方让渡权利，服从共同主权以求和平。
ideas.vEn: Each surrenders rights to a common sovereign in exchange for peace.

ideas.v: 主权者如人造的巨人，以威权维系秩序。
ideas.vEn: The sovereign is an artificial giant whose awe keeps order.

quotes.q: 人的生活孤独、贫困、卑污、残忍而短寿。
quotes.qEn: The life of man is solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short.

name: 让-雅克·卢梭
oneLiner: 人生而自由却无往不在枷锁之中；主权在民，法律应出自公意。
oneLinerEn: Man is born free yet everywhere in chains; sovereignty rests with the people and law should flow from the general will.
bio: 生于日内瓦的法国思想家，著《社会契约论》《爱弥儿》《忏悔录》。他批判私有制与文明使人堕落，主张人本善良而被社会败坏；以「公意」立国、主权在民，并倡导顺应天性的自然教育，深刻影响了法国大革命、现代民主与教育思想。
bioEn: Geneva-born French thinker behind The Social Contract, Emile and the Confessions. He critiqued property and civilization as corrupting, held that people are naturally good but spoiled by society, founded the state on the 'general will' with popular sovereignty, and urged education that follows nature — shaping the French Revolution, modern democracy and educational thought.

ideas.v: 主权在人民共同的意志，而非私利之和。
ideas.vEn: Sovereignty lies in the common will of the people, not the sum of private interests.

ideas.v: 自由是人的天性，枷锁来自不合理的制度。
ideas.vEn: Liberty is our nature; the chains come from unjust institutions.

ideas.v: 顺应儿童天性，多体验、少灌输。
ideas.vEn: Follow the child's nature; give experience, not cramming.

quotes.q: 人生而自由，却无往不在枷锁之中。
quotes.qEn: Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains.

name: 黑格尔
oneLiner: 现实与历史在矛盾与否定中层层上扬，精神逐步认识到自身而达于自由。
oneLinerEn: Reality and history rise through contradiction and negation as Spirit comes to know itself and so attains freedom.
bio: 德国哲学家，德国唯心论的集大成者。他以「辩证法」理解现实与历史：任何确定的观念都内含自身的矛盾，经由否定而被扬弃、上升到更高的统一。其《精神现象学》《法哲学原理》《历史哲学讲演录》深刻影响了马克思、存在主义与整个近代思想。
bioEn: German philosopher and culmination of German Idealism. He read reality and history dialectically: every determinate idea carries its own contradiction and, through negation, is sublated into a higher unity. His Phenomenology of Spirit, Philosophy of Right and Lectures on the Philosophy of History deeply shaped Marx, existentialism and much of modern thought.

ideas.v: 肯定内含否定，经否定之否定而达更高统一。
ideas.vEn: Each position holds its own negation and, through it, rises to a higher unity.

ideas.v: 既被取消又被保存，在更高层面被保留。
ideas.vEn: At once cancelled and preserved, kept on a higher level.

ideas.v: 历史借个人的激情来实现其自身的进程。
ideas.vEn: History works out its own course through the passions of individuals.

works.title: 法哲学原理
works.titleEn: Elements of the Philosophy of Right

quotes.q: 凡是合乎理性的都是现实的，凡是现实的都是合乎理性的。
quotes.qEn: What is rational is actual, and what is actual is rational.

name: 荀子
oneLiner: 人之性恶，其善者伪也——善不是天生，而是后天以礼义「化性起伪」雕琢出来的成就。
oneLinerEn: Human nature is crooked; the good in us is 'crafted'—not innate but wrought by ritual and rightness.
bio: 战国末期儒家大师。与孟子道性善相反，荀子主张「性恶」：人生而有欲，顺之则争夺残贼、归于混乱，故善并非天生，而靠师法教化与礼义「化性起伪」——以人为的努力改造天然材质。他隆礼重法、明分使群、劝学不息，又讲「天人之分」：天道不为圣君尧而存、不为暴君桀而亡，人当「制天命而用之」。有趣的是，他的弟子韩非、李斯竟走向法家，正见其礼法之间的巨大张力。
bioEn: The great Confucian master of the late Warring States. Against Mencius's innate goodness, Xunzi held human nature to be crooked: born with desires, we would fall into strife if we followed them, so the good is given but made—wrought by teachers, models and ritual through 'transforming nature and evoking artifice.' He exalted ritual and law, drew distinctions to bind society into groups, urged ceaseless learning, and separated Heaven from human affairs—the Way of Heaven persists not for the sage Yao nor perishes for the tyrant Jie; one should 'master Heaven and make use of it.' Strangely, his own students Han Fei and Li Si turned to Legalism, laying bare the tension within his blend of ritual and law.

ideas.v: 顺天然之欲则争乱，善有待于后天人为。
ideas.vEn: Following innate desires breeds strife; the good awaits deliberate making.

ideas.v: 以师法礼义改造本性，「伪」即人为的功夫。
ideas.vEn: By teaching and ritual one remolds raw nature; 'artifice' is the earned work of effort.

ideas.v: 天道运行不以人事为转移，人当各自尽分。
ideas.vEn: Heaven's course does not shift with human affairs; each should fulfil his own charge.

quotes.q: 人之性恶，其善者伪也。
quotes.qEn: Human nature is crooked; its goodness is deliberate artifice.

name: 墨子
oneLiner: 兼相爱、交相利——以无差等的互爱互利，反对以大吞小的不义之战。
oneLinerEn: Mutual care and mutual benefit—love without graded distinction, against wars that let the strong swallow the weak.
bio: 墨家创始人，出身工匠，代表「万民之利」发声。他主张「兼爱」：天下之乱起于「别相恶、交相贼」，应以无差等的互爱取代儒家差等之爱，并落在「交相利」的实际福祉上。据此起出「非攻」，谴责兼并掠夺，更身体力行赴千里助小国守城。他还倡「尚贤」「尚同」「节用」「节葬」，提出检验言论的「三表法」，并重逻辑、几何、力学与光学（小孔成像），是先秦最富科学与论辩精神的学派。
bioEn: Founder of the Mohist school, of artisan birth, speaking for the benefit of the myriad people. He urged impartial care: the world's chaos springs from mutual discrimination and harm, so graded Confucian love should yield to love without distinction, grounded in real mutual benefit. From this came 'against offensive war'—denouncing annexation, which he resisted by hurrying a thousand li to help weak states hold their walls. He further championed exalting the worthy, frugality and simple funerals, set out the 'three criteria' for testing claims, and prized logic, geometry, mechanics and optics (pinhole imaging)—the most scientific and argumentative school of the age.

ideas.v: 视人之身若视其身，爱无差等。
ideas.vEn: Regard others' bodies as your own—love without grades.

ideas.v: 攻国为大不义，强不凌弱、众不劫寡。
ideas.vEn: Invading a state is the greatest injustice; the strong should not crush the weak.

ideas.v: 上本于古者圣王之事、下原察百姓耳目之实、发以为刑政观其中国家百姓之利。
ideas.vEn: Test claims against the sage-kings of old, the people's lived experience, and their benefit when made policy.

quotes.q: 兼相爱，交相利。
quotes.qEn: Mutual care, mutual benefit.

name: 莱布尼茨
oneLiner: 世界由无数「无窗」却能知觉的单子构成，彼此不相因果，却由神预先设定而和谐共舞。
oneLinerEn: Reality is made of countless windowless yet perceiving 'monads'—not causally interacting, but harmonized in advance by God to keep perfect step.
bio: 德国博学家：哲学家、数学家，与牛顿各自发明微积分，又创二进制、构想一种普遍的形式语言与组合逻辑。形而上学上，他把终极实在看作「单子」——无部分、不能自外来影响的单纯实体，各有其「知觉」与「趋求」的内在展开；单子之间「没有窗户」，看似相互作用，实则由神在创世时安排「前定和谐」，如两座各自精准却始终同步的钟。他以「充足理由律」要求凡事必有其所以然之理，并由此论证神存在、断言我们所居乃「一切可能世界中最好的一个」。此说经伏尔泰借《老实人》讽刺里斯本地震而广受质疑，却始终是对「恶之问题」最雄心勃勃的回应之一。
bioEn: A German polymath—philosopher and mathematician—who invented the calculus alongside Newton, devised binary numbers and sketched a universal formal language and combinational logic. In metaphysics he took ultimate reality to be 'monads': simple, partless substances admitting no outside influence, each unfolding its own perceptions and appetitions. Monads have 'no windows'; they only appear to interact, being reconciled by God at creation through a 'pre-established harmony,' like two clocks each exact yet always in step. His principle of sufficient reason demands a 'why' for everything, and from it he argued for God and claimed this the 'best of all possible worlds'—a thesis Voltaire mocked in Candide over the Lisbon earthquake, yet still among the most ambitious answers to the problem of evil.

ideas.v: 无窗、无部分、能知觉的单纯实体，是实在之终极构成。
ideas.vEn: Windowless, partless, perceiving simple substances—the ultimate furniture of reality.

ideas.v: 单子不相因果交通，却因神预设而同步如两钟。
ideas.vEn: Monads do not causally interact yet keep step as two clocks, harmonized by God.

ideas.v: 凡有之事必有其所以如此而不如彼之理。
ideas.vEn: Nothing holds true without a why that makes it so rather than otherwise.

quotes.q: 在一切可能的世界中，神选择了最好的一个。
quotes.qEn: Of all possible worlds, God chose the best.

name: 克尔凯郭尔
oneLiner: 真理不是旁观的体系，而是主体在焦虑与抉择中「为我所真」地去承担——孤身成为自我。
oneLinerEn: Truth is not a spectator's system but what I stake myself on in anxiety and choice—becoming a self, alone.
bio: 丹麦思想家，被尊为存在主义之父。他反抗黑格尔把个人化入「体系」的非人视角：生活的关键是单个的人如何成为真正的自我，而这并非客观思辨所能给出。他剖析生存的「诸阶段」——沉溺当下的审美、承担义务的伦理、以及凌驾普遍、独自面对上帝的信仰；三者之间须靠「抉择」的跳跃贯通，理性无法代劳。他以众多笔名写出畏、绝望、罪与信仰的悖论（亚伯拉罕献以撒，超越伦理而踏入信仰），并抨击「基督教国度」把信仰稀释成体面的常情。对后世海德格尔、萨特与整个存在主义影响深远。
bioEn: A Danish thinker hailed as the father of existentialism. He rebelled against Hegel dissolving the individual into an impersonal 'system': what matters is how the single person becomes a real self—something objective speculation cannot hand over. He dissected the 'stages' of existence—aesthetic absorption in the moment, ethical commitment to duty, and faith that, set above the universal, stands alone before God; passage among them requires the leap of choice, which reason cannot do for you. Under many pseudonyms he wrote of dread, despair, sin and the paradox of faith (Abraham offering Isaac, stepping beyond ethics into faith), and he attacked 'Christendom' for thinning faith into respectable convention. His mark on Heidegger, Sartre and all later existentialism is deep.

ideas.v: 最要紧的真理不在客观确证，而在主体以无限激情去承担。
ideas.vEn: The truth that matters is not objective certainty but the self's passionate, infinite appropriation of it.

ideas.v: 审美—伦理—信仰三层，其间须有非理性的抉择。
ideas.vEn: Aesthetic, ethical, religious—each reached not by inference but by a choice beyond reason.

ideas.v: 面对悖论与畏，纵身投入，而非坐候证据齐备。
ideas.vEn: Facing paradox and dread one casts oneself, rather than waiting for the evidence to be in.

quotes.q: 必须找到那个我为之而生、为之而死的思想。
quotes.qEn: What I need is to find the thought I dare live and die for.

name: 伯特兰·罗素
oneLiner: 把哲学交给逻辑分析：以摹状词理论解开指称之谜，也用「罗素悖论」撼动数学的地基。
oneLinerEn: He put philosophy into logical analysis—untying reference with the theory of descriptions and shaking mathematics' foundations with Russell's paradox.
bio: 英国哲学家、逻辑学家与公共知识人，1950 年诺贝尔文学奖得主。他与怀特海合著《数学原理》，试图把数学还原为逻辑；所提「罗素悖论」（一切不属于自身的集合之集合）暴露了朴素集合论的破绽，逼出公理化与类型论。他更以「摹状词理论」把「当今的法国国王是秃头」这类限定描绘短语析解为「存在且唯一」的逻辑结构，被视为分析哲学的典范。晚年多写社会与伦理议题（《我为什么不是基督徒》），因反战入狱，又投身反核、推动《罗素—爱因斯坦宣言》；一生兼具冷静的逻辑与对世事的炽热关切。
bioEn: British philosopher, logician and public intellectual, Nobel laureate in Literature (1950). With Whitehead he wrote Principia Mathematica, aiming to reduce mathematics to logic; his paradox—the set of all sets that are not members of themselves—exposed a crack in naive set theory and forced axiomatization and a theory of types. His theory of descriptions resolved a definite description such as 'the present King of France is bald' into a logical structure of existence-and-uniqueness—an exemplar of analytic philosophy. Late in life he turned to society and ethics (Why I Am Not a Christian), was jailed for his pacifism, and pressed the anti-nuclear cause behind the Russell–Einstein Manifesto—cool logic wedded all his life to a burning concern for the world.

ideas.v: 「当今法国国王」不作名称而作逻辑描状，消解指空之谜。
ideas.vEn: A phrase like 'the present King of France' is not a name but a logical description, dissolving puzzles of reference to the nonexistent.

ideas.v: 「不属于自身的集合之集合」自相矛盾，撼动朴素集合论。
ideas.vEn: The set of all sets not members of themselves contradicts itself, shaking naive set theory.

ideas.v: 世界是事实的总和，命题可析解为逻辑原子。
ideas.vEn: The world is the totality of facts; propositions resolve into logical atoms.

quotes.q: 参差多态，乃是幸福的本源。
quotes.qEn: Variety is essential to happiness.
